Decide the layout and emit the markdown block for one table (docx/html)

Source: R/quarto-table.R
apa_quarto_markdown_block.Rd

The non-PDF counterpart of `apa_quarto_latex_block()`: same ladder (`apa_layout_decide()`), same "rotate before shrink" policy, but the output is a pandoc grid table (`apa_markdown_table()`) rather than raw LaTeX, and a font-size choice below the default becomes a STYLE MARKER (D38, Route A) rather than per-cell markup.

Usage

apa_quarto_markdown_block(x, font.size = NULL, title = NULL, note = NULL)

Arguments

x

an apaTables table or spec.

font.size

optional explicit point size, overriding the ladder (D26).

title

optional table title, overriding the one apaTables generated, as the `title` argument shared by `apa.quarto.pdf()` / `apa.quarto.docx()` / `apa.quarto.html()` does on the LaTeX path too. A chunk's `tbl-cap` still wins over this (D22, resolved by the filter, not here).

note

optional table note, overriding the one apaTables generated, mirroring `title` above. A chunk's `apa-note` still wins over this.

Value

a `knit_asis` object.

Details

Rotation in Word is DECIDED BY MEASUREMENT by default (D32), but Phase 1.7 (Task 3) makes the `landscape =` argument – carried on `x$landscape` – a binding tri-state override. It is resolved against the chunk option by `apa_landscape_request()`: chunk option first, then the argument, then `NA` meaning "measurement decides". The two Quarto destinations still agree with each other, and with PDF (`apa_quarto_latex_block()`), because both now read the same precedence.

Title and note (Task 7) are attached the same way `apa_quarto_latex_block()` relies on its caller to attach them – `apa_meta_div_for()`, an empty `::: {.apa-table-meta}` div read by the bundled `apatablemeta.lua`. That filter is registered `at: post-quarto` in `_extension.yml`'s COMMON filter list, so it already runs on this destination too (never reimplemented or branched on precedence here; see that function's own comment for why). Unlike the LaTeX path, where `apa_quarto_render()` (Task 8; `apa.quarto. table()` did this before it was retired, D30) combines the two outside `apa_quarto_latex_block()`, here the div is appended INSIDE this function. This is the one function every non-PDF entry point (Task 8) and every fixture in this suite already calls directly.
